name: Kalyani Cast-Tech Limited
summary: Hold — unresolved. BQS 5.2, GQS 5.0 after persistent cash-realization cap, IAS NS. Real specialty-container economics and Gujarat milestones, but group cash/NCI reliability, current expansion funding and complete implementation evidence remain unresolved. Ordinary and non-rescue return/entry fields are null; rescue cases are explicit counterfactuals, not recommendations.

GQS.override: CASH 3 persistent realization weakness caps GQS at 5

ranking_eligibility.reason: G2 financial-reliability Hold; IAS also incomplete.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: No verified integrity hard stop. Family RPTs, repeated corrections and funding/allocation opacity require monitoring. Published clarifications and clean audit findings are counterevidence; no fraud allegation.
gates.resolution: Reconcile Section 186 wording, provide ownership/capital-allocation record and confirm current encumbrance/lock-ins.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Material unresolved group cash-classification and subsidiary consolidation/ownership bridge. Cash totals reconcile and full audit/control reports are unmodified, but those do not supply the missing elimination and NCI cash ledger.
gates.resolution: Issuer/auditor consolidated cash-flow reclassification bridge for FY24–26; KMT ownership/allotment and intercompany elimination schedule; correction/clarification of AS23 policy wording. Quantify rather than assume misstatement.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Current phase spending and resources cannot be verified against ₹35 crore remaining commitments and corrected July plan. Scenarios breach cash before entry. No reported default is alleged.
gates.resolution: Latest published consolidated liquidity and debt maturity/utilization data, remaining project costs including capital creditors, facility purposes/availability and downside funding headroom.

gates.name: Tradability and implementation
gates.reason: Lot verified but complete dated exchange trading values, current restrictions and spreads unresolved. Secondary close is not executable.
gates.resolution: Validate 60-session BSE tape including zero/no-print dates, surveillance/lot/lock-in status and practical whole-lot execution at actual position size.

material_facts: Promoter funding commitment includes an actual 25% warrant receipt, with pricing and capital changes disclosed.
Family RPTs and repeated corrective filings require discipline monitoring; director remuneration ₹0.86 crore is modest relative to PAT.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Unmodified audit/control opinions and explicit corrections counter a misconduct inference.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed stewardship: positive funding and disclosure response, but capital-allocation payback, inconsistent Section 186 narrative and minority/perimeter transparency are not strong enough for 7+.

material_facts: Specialty stainless and logistics-oriented container designs have delivered units.
Top seven customers accounted for 97% of FY23 product sales without firm long-term volume contracts.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Rail qualification, location and repeat customer relationships are useful barriers; no independently measured structural cost advantage or exclusive IP established.
factor_audit.rationale: A differentiated niche, not a demonstrated durable monopoly; larger wagon incumbents and customer buying power keep advantage contestable.

material_facts: Comparable FY23–26 reported revenue CAGR 33.32%.
FY26 growth only 7.70%, with goods sales down 2.29% and service/unbilled lines supplying the increase.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Container pivot makes FY21 trough unsuitable; underlying unit/price history and current mix bridge are incomplete.
factor_audit.rationale: Starting schedule 9 at ≥30%; no discretionary trajectory adjustment, then Medium-confidence/history ceiling 8. Window chosen for comparability, not to maximize score.

material_facts: Gujarat container capacity, trial train and formal ICD LoI create real adjacent demand access.
Six-month GCT approval and uncommissioned wagon/ICD activities constrain timing and customer capture.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Domestic rail logistics and specialty products offer avenues beyond the current base, but management TAM and ₹4,000–5,000 crore ambition are not orders.
factor_audit.rationale: Accessible but execution- and approval-dependent runway, stronger than a speculative idea but short of repeated demonstrated profitable scale.

material_facts: Organic full-group FY23–25 incremental ROIC about 17.20%, versus 13–16% assumed capital cost.
Including FY26 expansion reduces FY23–26 bridge to 10.46%; single-year incremental return 4.20%.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: CWIP, project lag and new subsidiary capacity make a one-year low ratio premature evidence of persistent destruction.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed incremental economics, not NS merely because project cohorts are unavailable. Entire organic capital base and NCI included; 5 reflects uncertain maturation, not a neutral imputation or a current ROCE proxy.

material_facts: Three-year CFO/PAT 0.415 and five-year 0.534 remain poor.
FY26 improvement relies on inventory release and customer advances; ₹6.88 crore aged over a year persists.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY26 CFO genuinely recovered to ₹18.22 crore; bank submissions agree with books.
factor_audit.rationale: Persistent cash-realization weakness, not only a one-period expansion build. GQS cap 5 is triggered; no assertion that customer advances are improper revenue.

material_facts: March debt is only ₹0.578 crore and cash plus lower-valued investments about ₹7.10 crore.
₹35 crore remaining capital commitments and overlapping larger expansion plans exceed readily evidenced discretionary resources; non-rescue cash stress breaches the floor.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: HDFC sanctioned WC ceiling and ₹4.70 crore later warrant deposit are real supports; no reported default, and unverified funding is not proof of insolvency.
factor_audit.rationale: Funding fragility is evidenced enough for a low factor, while current solvency remains unresolved. No invented project borrowing or subsidy receipt.

material_facts: Container and terminal milestones reached actual physical delivery/trial operation.
FY26 ₹180–200 crore management revenue discussion missed; dated terminal and ICD approvals followed earlier expected June timing.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Steel disruptions and selective orders are management explanations; material innovations and August operation are counterevidence.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed milestone delivery with some real follow-through. Ceremonial schedule movement and the whole long-term campus aspiration are not scored as fulfilled commercial commitments.

material_facts: Parent PAT rose to ₹17.08 crore with positive underlying EBIT.
Higher MF gain and absence of prior liquidated damages explain about 59% of PBT growth; unbilled/services changes complicate recurrence.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: All-other-income-excluded normalized parent PAT remains about ₹15.48 crore and shares did not expand during FY26.
factor_audit.rationale: Operating profitability is real, but recurring per-share earnings growth is mixed; avoid conflating this factor with cash conversion.

material_facts: A full five-year sector model and 12/15/18% entry sensitivity are reproducible.
Current financing and project spending bridge is not substantiated; all non-rescue paths breach pre-entry cash.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Explicit rescue cases are modeled, but their availability and dilution cannot be treated as the ordinary shareholder forecast.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: no supported ordinary IRR. The numeric rescue IRR is not inserted into the return-spread rubric.

material_facts: Credible stress requires additional equity; bear rescue terminal value is about 19% of entry price.
Only limited cash and a small book base support an approximately ₹807 crore quoted equity value.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Operating business is profitable and little funded debt reduces creditor pressure; rescue bull retains upside.
factor_audit.rationale: Material permanent-loss and recapitalization risk at the price. A low downside-resilience score is supported even though a precise ordinary-return distribution is unknown.

material_facts: Base rescue economics do not meet 15%, even after strong core growth and new verticals.
Funded reverse model requires roughly 47.7% core growth plus large equity issuance under base exit assumptions.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull scenario can exceed the hurdle, demonstrating possibility rather than impossibility; better ownership or multiples help.
factor_audit.rationale: Several optimistic execution assumptions must coincide. This is price-implied expectations, not business predictability; reverse solution is explicitly counterfactual and ownership-sensitive.

material_facts: Official lot verified at 250 shares; two providers match the dated close.
Twenty- and sixty-observation capacity calculations are available but not complete verified exchange turnover/restriction evidence.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Secondary tape indicates activity and a short theoretical exit time; lot indivisibility and one-sided circuits can dominate.
factor_audit.rationale: NS until official or sufficiently validated full trading calendar, traded values, current restrictions and spreads support a canonical point. Missing dates are not zero trades.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Kalyani Cast-Tech is a real, profitable specialty-container manufacturer making an ambitious move into wagons and rail-linked logistics. The opportunity is more credible than a presentation-only project: container delivery, a first terminal trial train, a railway notification and an ICD letter-of-intent approval all exist. They do not yet establish permanent terminal permissions, full wagon commissioning, customer economics or a funded ₹450–500 crore programme.

Business Quality Score is 5.2/10; Growth Quality Score is 5.0/10 after the persistent cash-realization override. IAS is NS. The quality points are analytical diagnostics, excluded from comparative rankings while G2 remains on Hold. This is not a compounder designation or an investment recommendation.

At the historical 19 October close of ₹1,123.85, quoted equity value is approximately ₹806.98 crore, or 47.2 times FY26 parent earnings. Three-year CFO/PAT is only 0.42. Ordinary IRRs and entry prices are null: unknown current funding and pre-entry cash gaps cannot be repaired by silently assuming future warrant cash, project debt or subsidy. Separate fully specified rescue counterfactuals show approximately −28.1%, −3.0% and +17.4% five-year returns in bear/base/bull cases. Their purpose is to reveal the cost of financing and execution, not to offer targets. The published HDFC facility is assessed as a potential resource, not dismissed: a conditional collateral-based drawing-power test supports some phase funding, but normalized-cash and stress cases still show gaps.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Company: Kalyani Cast-Tech Limited. ISIN INE0N6U01018. BSE SME security 544023; official interoperable master symbol KALYANI$. Latest legal CIN in current filings is L30200DL2012PLC242760; older financial-note templates retain historical codes. This is not Kalyani Commercials, Kalyani Steels, Bharat Forge or an assumed NSE listing. Master SM and ST rows are retained as evidence, not interpreted as unrestricted listing permissions.

Information cutoff is 20 October 2026. Market reference is 19 October, retrieved later but filtered to the cutoff; subsequent quotes are excluded. Latest audited full year is 31 March 2026. No September 2026 financial results have been used. Financials are INR crore, with issuer lakh values divided by 100; price is rupees and share counts are actual shares. Return convention is nominal pretax, five calendar years, with a 15% equity hurdle and 12%/18% sensitivity. ₹5 lakh is an illustrative implementation amount, not a suitable allocation for this user.

G1 Conditional: no proven integrity hard stop, but stewardship questions remain. G2 Hold: consolidation/NCI and cash-classification bridges need resolution despite clean audits. G3 Hold: current project financeability not established. G4 Hold: complete trading-value and restriction evidence missing. Confidence is Medium for historical operating economics and Low for current funding availability/project maturity. Missing inputs remain unknown, rather than receiving neutral scores or being presumed adverse events.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Factor points: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5; R NS, D 3, P 3 and L NS. Each factor audit includes at least two material facts, contrary evidence, source/evidence links and a scoring rationale. No high score is awarded for disclosure volume, management ambition or an attractive narrative.

BQS uses 20% GOV + 20% MOAT + 12% REV + 10% DUR + 12% CAP + 10% CASH + 8% BAL + 8% EXEC = 5.18, displayed 5.2. GQS is 40% REV + 20% DUR + 15% EARN + 15% CAP + 10% CASH = 6.20; CASH 3 reflects persistent multi-year realization weakness, so the final value is capped at 5.0. This override does not allege persistent destruction from immature capex.

IAS uses unrounded final BQS ×25%, R ×35%, D ×20%, P ×10%, L ×10%. Its known contribution is 2.1950, coverage 55%, and missing-factor bound 2.6450–6.6950. It remains NS, never renormalized or replaced by that interval midpoint. Decimal arithmetic and half-up display rounding are embedded. G2 excludes all quality, growth and investment ranking flags even though BQS/GQS factor coverage is complete.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company began with steel/iron castings and railway components, then expanded container manufacturing, including dwarf, double-stack, automotive and specialty stainless-steel products. FY26 reported goods sales were ₹135.86 crore, services ₹8.67 crore, unbilled revenue ₹5.00 crore, rental revenue ₹0.42 crore and a small freight balance. Domestic sales dominate; the financial-note export line is nil. Services and unbilled items cannot be assumed to have the same recurrence or cash profile as container shipments.

Its economic proposition is to reduce customers’ transportation costs through container design, payload, space utilization and reduced empty repositioning. Customers include rail/logistics and industrial users; customer purchase orders rather than enforceable multi-year minimum volumes govern much of the business. Steel, fabrication, power and working capital are important inputs. The cost base and order selection are vulnerable to steel price and freight disruptions.

The Gujarat campus combines manufacturing with rail access, a GCT and a proposed ICD. KMT Engineering is a controlled organic subsidiary incorporated in February 2024, not a purchased mature business. Subsidiary investment and loans are intra-group balances and are not additive group cash or enterprise value. The report models core manufacturing, new wagon revenue and logistics separately; it does not value operational land again on top of enterprise value. Current legal ownership percentages and exact allocation of new operations among parent/KMT remain questions, so conservative attribution and an alternative ownership sensitivity are explicit.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Design skill, railway familiarity, qualified manufacturing processes and location near Kandla/Mundra create useful differentiation. The May letter reports delivery of 56 stainless-steel units and describes specialized bulk-salt, chemical and automotive designs. The first trial train and actual infrastructure permissions add credibility to the integrated manufacturing/logistics proposition. These are management-reported product achievements and authority-backed access milestones, not independent proof of exclusive intellectual property or a permanent cost advantage.

Buyer power is important: the prospectus disclosed 97% of FY23 product sales to seven customers and no firm long-term volume commitment from many key buyers. FY26 receivables are concentrated too; one corporate debtor accounts for about ₹18.42 crore and another aged balance for ₹6.42 crore, together about three quarters of total receivables including unbilled balances. No current customer revenue concentration bridge was retrieved. Customization can support repeat business, but concentrated procurement can also force pricing and payment concessions.

The wagon opportunity is contested. Titagarh reported 9,431 wagons in FY25 with capacity around 12,000; Texmaco’s broad rolling-stock business reported strong production growth. These firms possess scale, approvals, supplier relationships and operating history that Kalyani has not yet demonstrated in wagons. Their diversified revenue/margins are not a clean peer-multiple benchmark. MOAT 5 recognizes a useful niche while requiring customer retention, realized cost savings, independent design protection and repeat gross margins before calling it structural.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Historical operating revenue is ₹11.20/49.45/63.27/94.48/139.22/149.94 crore for FY21–FY26. Three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 33.32%. Five-year CAGR is 68.01%, but FY21 is a COVID/foundry trough preceding the container pivot, so it is shown rather than scored as comparable demand. Ten-year history is unavailable. KMT is organic development, not an acquired operating sales base; changing group mix still limits comparability.

FY26 growth was 7.70%, versus about 47% in FY25. The audited result presents H1 FY26 revenue ₹92.3970 crore and balancing H2 ₹57.5477 crore; compared with ₹70.2150/69.0079 crore for FY25, growth was approximately +31.59%/−16.61%. H2 is annual audited less limited-reviewed H1, not a separately audited quarter. Goods revenue actually fell 2.29%; services increased by ₹8.51 crore and ₹5 crore unbilled revenue appeared. A full units × average selling price reconciliation has not been published in the retrieved financials. The existing container line’s strength therefore cannot be inferred merely from total reported top-line growth. Management attributes second-half weakness to steel-price increases, selective order refusal and geopolitical disruptions.

The latest September filing specifies approximately 10,000 TEUs annual capacity and 2,400 wagons prospective capacity. Earlier communications use different container scopes and 2,500 wagons. They cannot be added together without a site/unit reconciliation. Our annual model exposes TEU-equivalent volumes at an illustrative ₹2.6 lakh per TEU and wagon units at ₹30 lakh per wagon. These are operating cross-check assumptions, not issuer price guidance; the base terminal core scale exceeds the September demonstrated capacity and requires further investment. REV begins at 9 under the ≥30% schedule and is capped at 8 by Medium confidence, without an extra base-distortion penalty.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is broader than before, but its maturity differs. Container manufacturing and a terminal trial train exist. Wagon operations in the 11 September filing are still expected to begin subject to approvals. The ICD has a letter-of-intent approval, not completed customs infrastructure or an operating notification. GCT permission is temporary and requires a fresh proposal after specified work. Refrigerated-container technology cooperation is signed, while its proposed reciprocal investment is not cash received.

The incremental capital bridge avoids substituting a current ROCE headline for CAP. At a normalized 25.17% tax rate, operating NOPAT increases from ₹8.16 crore in FY23 to ₹15.47 crore in FY26; whole-group invested capital including NCI, CWIP and advances increases from ₹14.16 crore to ₹84.08 crore. That gives 10.46% incremental return, compared with 17.20% for FY23–25. The 13–16% capital-cost range is an analytical hurdle, not a reported company WACC. A 3% revenue cash reserve is retained when separating operating from financial capital. An independent asset-side bridge sums PPE, intangibles, CWIP/development, capital advances, other noncurrent assets, deferred tax and operating current assets, less trade/other liabilities and provisions, plus required cash. Across all six years it matches financing-side IC within ₹0.0002 crore of source rounding; both full bridges are embedded.

This supports CAP 5, not NS or a high-return project claim: the organic bridge is coherent but maturation is uncertain. Pre-commissioning investment depresses the latest ratio, and the earlier operating business did generate better returns. Conversely, the June 2025 call did not establish a calculated programme payback. The binding near-term funding anchor is ₹35 crore remaining capital commitments net of advances; the corrected ₹70 crore phase, ₹110 crore registered terminal project and ₹450–500 crore longer-term programme are overlapping scopes, not additive obligations. GQS is capped at 5 because cash conversion has been persistently weak, not because every expansion rupee is assumed wasted.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder experience and product development are important strengths. Actual output and physical milestones prevent dismissing the business as merely promotional. Stewardship nevertheless needs a more precise capital allocation and disclosure record. FY26 director remuneration was ₹0.8595 crore, about 5% of parent PAT, versus ₹0.685 crore a year earlier. Family rent, legal services and labour/service transactions are disclosed. Management describes them as ordinary-course, arm’s-length transactions subject to approvals, and the audit reports compliance; independent commercial benchmarking was not available.

The May investor letter incorrectly described ₹70 crore as invested in FY26. The 8 June clarification explicitly recast it as a plan, only partly incurred, with balance targeted by July. This response must be retained alongside the original claim. The report does not infer fraudulent intent from the correction, but execution claims must now reconcile cash deployment and asset commissioning. November 2025 discussion of ₹180–200 crore FY26 revenue was not delivered: actual operating revenue was ₹149.94 crore. Railway/ICD approvals arrived after earlier June expectations, with steel and geopolitical explanations supplied by management. A one-day ceremonial change is not treated as an operational failure.

Warrants were allotted at ₹582 with ₹4.70 crore received. Full exercise is optional and adds 323,123 shares; total count expansion is 4.50%, existing-holder dilution 4.306%, with promoter percentage increasing to about 61.19%. July and August corrections were made after exchange observations about subscriber classification and percentage columns, and the company confirms shareholder approval. Their existence is a disclosure-quality concern, not a proved regulatory offence. The directors’ report statement that no Section 186 loans/investments were made conflicts in presentation with detailed KMT funding disclosures and needs a scope explanation. G1 therefore remains Conditional, not a proven integrity fail.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Cash and earnings: FY21 PAT exceeded PBT because of a deferred-tax benefit, so its profit percentage is not a clean growth base. Reported EPS uses historical weighted-average shares, while a separate end-of-period-share EPS removes denominator ambiguity; FY24 IPO-year reported EPS ₹16.42 differs from ₹13.36 at year-end shares. FY26 consolidated CFO of ₹18.22 crore exceeded total PAT of ₹17.11 crore, but three-year CFO of ₹17.01 crore trails cumulative PAT of ₹40.96 crore. Five-year conversion is only 0.53. FY26 CFO includes inventory liquidation of ₹3.765 crore and ₹5.8892 crore additional customer advances; subtracting those two sources leaves ₹8.5691 crore. This is a diagnostic, not a claim those legitimate advances are improper. Receivables used ₹6.58 crore and other current assets ₹3.91 crore, including a large GST-credit build. Three-year cash capex including advances totals ₹45.74 crore and resulting free cash flow is negative ₹28.73 crore.

Ageing and profit quality: ₹6.4242 crore receivables sit 1–2 years past due, ₹0.4573 crore are disputed beyond three years and ₹5 crore is unbilled. Together over-year balances plus unbilled equal about 36% of receivables. Management considers them recoverable; that is counterevidence, not a collection receipt. A ₹0.0721 crore bad-debt charge exists despite no doubtful provision in the closing ageing grid. Mutual-fund gains increased by ₹1.255 crore and prior ₹0.8738 crore liquidated damages disappeared; together those effects explain about 59% of incremental PBT. Removing all other income still leaves roughly ₹15.48 crore normalized parent PAT.

Complete audit package: the main FY26 standalone and consolidated opinions, separate IFC opinions and explicit audit-trail paragraphs are unmodified/positive. CARO says quarterly stock/book-debt submissions agree with books, reports HDFC sanction ₹23.38 crore versus drawing about ₹0.578 crore, and identifies no default or material fraud. FY25 equivalents are also positive, with ₹17.45 crore sanctioned and ₹5.2763 crore drawn. There is no reported quantified bank reconciliation exception. A generic FY26 cross-reference to a modification is inconsistent with the explicit positive audit-trail paragraph and is not called a substantive audit-trail failure. These details were read, not inferred from the main opinion alone.

Unresolved consolidation/cash presentation: FY26 CFO subtracts ₹0.0302 crore NCI profit and investing contains ₹4.0402 crore NCI movement. Reclassifying algebraically preserves total cash: CFO ₹18.2535 crore, CFI −₹23.9822 crore and CFF −₹0.7816 crore, using an inferred ₹4.01 crore outside contribution. This is not an issuer restatement. FY25 investing instead contains the entire ₹0.4926 crore closing NCI despite only ₹0.0106 crore year-on-year increase, and a ₹0.5847 crore investment outflow with zero consolidated investment balances. CARO explains the parent’s ₹0.51 crore subscription payment against prior payable but not the complete group eliminations. The consolidation policy incorrectly describes AS23/equity method for a subsidiary while the balance sheet eliminates the parent investment/loan. A current ownership/cash-elimination schedule is needed, particularly because new operations are central to value. Net cash closes, so no missing cash or fraud is alleged; G2 Hold reflects unresolved reliability/comparability, not normal standalone-versus-consolidated differences.

Other balances: mutual-fund book value exceeds disclosed fair value by ₹0.10981 crore, a bounded question under the stated policy; valuation uses the lower amount. ₹0.0555 crore pledged FD is excluded from available cash. ₹0.2658 crore gratuity is retained as a terminal deduction. Electricity litigation exposure is ₹0.4852 crore, not reported tax arrears; the bear case pays it. Existing operating leases remain in expense margins rather than creating duplicate lease debt. Subsidiary equity/loan funding is eliminated, NCI retained, and no separate operational property value added.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹1,123.85, historical equity capitalization is ₹806.98 crore, reported P/E 47.25 and all-other-income-excluded P/E 52.13. Historical book multiple is 9.88. These combine a dated October quote and March financials, not a claim about current enterprise value or executable price. Peer operating comparisons are used for competitive context; no unverified current peer-multiple average sets fair value.

The linked model runs from 31 March 2026 through the 19 October entry bridge to 19 October 2031. It splits FY27 before/after entry and interpolates the terminal FY31/FY32 operating run rate with actual day counts, including the FY32 leap-year denominator. No post-terminal cash gap changes the investor horizon. Base core revenue grows 18%, with staged wagon/logistics revenue, 14.5%/13%/30% EBITDA margins and 10×/10×/12× exit EV/EBITDA. Bear and bull have distinct volumes, margins, working capital, capex and multiples. Required operating cash is 3% of revenue, retained in terminal equity; cash less reserve is signed, never floored away. A normalized P/E cross-check uses 12×/18×/22×. DCF is not forced on immature, funding- and perimeter-uncertain projects.

Current financing is unverified, so ordinary return and entry fields are null. Non-rescue paths also remain null after pre-entry cash breaches, rather than being displayed as if negative cash were free debt. Rescue models separately raise equity at 70% of the reference quote, deduct 2% fees, issue explicit shares and distinguish deposit from optional warrant exercise. Base rescue requires ₹23.42 crore gross new money and ends with 7.96% dilution versus current holders including warrants. Its counterfactual terminal value is ₹966.14 per share, IRR -2.98%; the P/E cross-check is ₹1169.27. Neither is an ordinary target. New-vertical economics receive a conservative 51% parent attribution, with 70% sensitivity, because current legal ownership was not conclusively verified; all group cash surplus is conservatively haircut at that share while deficits remain fully deducted.

Stress tables change working capital, margins, capex, multiples, warrant exercise and ownership and contain complete annual funding rows. A separate 4×3 core-growth/exit-multiple grid reruns financing for every cell. The historical EV/EBITDA screen excludes a market NCI claim and is explicitly only a lower-bound, non-comparable diagnostic, not a clean enterprise multiple. The base counterfactual entries at 12%/15%/18% are ₹548.21/₹480.34/₹422.31, not actionable buy levels. A capital-scaled reverse solver checks a real funded crossing; around 47.7% annual core growth is required to meet 15% under base exits, involving approximately ₹1,573 crore terminal revenue and ₹151 crore equity rescue. Ordinary implied growth is null. Optimistic assumptions could deliver upside, but the present price offers little demonstrated margin for error.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The principal permanent-loss sequence is not high existing debt. It is capital consumption ahead of recurring revenue: cash is deployed into unfinished infrastructure, old receivables fail to clear, customer advances normalize, approvals or wagon orders lag, and fresh equity becomes necessary when market sentiment is weaker. A low March debt number does not protect current shareholders from that sequence. Conversely, the ₹23.38 crore published WC facility is meaningful: excluding all unbilled and over-one-year receivables and applying a 25% collateral haircut yields an assumed ₹19.02 crore additional-draw ceiling. A one-year resource test using reported CFO has about ₹7.41 crore headroom after commitments, reserve, litigation and interest; stripping inventory/customer-advance releases creates about ₹2.25 crore shortfall, and a 50% collateral haircut worsens it to ₹8.24 crore. These are availability/purpose/timing assumptions, not assertions that the bank refused funding. Linked full-year draw counterfactuals still breach the cash floor later in the horizon. The most severe shortfall can occur before the modeled purchase date; models cannot retroactively assume funding existed.

The bear case holds core growth to 5%, uses 11% core EBITDA margin, delays new wagon/logistics sales, increases working capital to 30% of revenue, pays ₹0.4852 crore litigation exposure and exits at 7×/7×/8× EBITDA. Even with explicit cash-floor rescue, the counterfactual terminal price is about ₹216, an approximately 81% loss from the reference quote and −28.1% annual return. Its gross equity rescue is about ₹37.32 crore. Those are scenarios, not forecasts or a claim of actual insolvency. Without the rescue, return fields are null because the path is not financeable.

Additional risks are buyer concentration, a large specific aged debtor, misestimated project costs, steel squeeze, regulatory continuation of a temporary terminal, delayed customs infrastructure, and public-market exit constraints. Book equity of ₹81.68 crore is not liquidation recovery and cannot be added to an operating multiple. Counterevidence matters: the core business has positive EBIT, low reported bank debt, legitimate customer advances, clean bank reconciliation reporting and real physical assets. Those reduce some creditor risk but do not prove protection of the purchase price or completion of the investment programme.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome from ₹1,123.85 is ₹5,619.25; tenfold is ₹11,238.50. With only the known warrants fully exercised, and before any additional rescue dilution, an 18× terminal parent P/E requires approximately ₹234.2 crore parent PAT for 5× and ₹468.5 crore for 10×. At a 10% parent-equivalent net margin this implies about ₹2342 crore and ₹4685 crore revenue equivalents respectively. These are transparent reverse hurdles, not predictions.

Relative to FY26 ₹149.94 crore revenue, the corresponding five-year annual expansion requirements are about 73.3% and 99.0%. Actual group revenue would need to be greater where NCI takes part of earnings, while new equity raises increase the required parent PAT further. Manufacturing capacity, railway approvals, order conversion, working capital and capex all have to scale together; market-cap arithmetic alone is not feasibility.

The company’s September ₹4,000–5,000 crore aspiration is numerically large enough to make an optimistic narrative sound plausible, but it is expressly contingent, lacks a validated funded annual bridge, and is far beyond the demonstrated base. The model’s bull case does not reach 5× despite a strong operating ramp. Classify both outcomes as unproven/highly demanding rather than impossible or probable. Evidence of sustained collections and profitable commissioned capacity must precede a multibagger designation.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Priority 1, financial reliability: obtain a consolidated FY24–26 cash-flow/NCI and subsidiary-elimination bridge, confirmation of KMT ownership and its capital receipts, and correction of the subsidiary accounting-policy wording. Reconcile investment/interest elimination and the small mutual-fund valuation difference. These are finite, specific disclosure requests, not a demand for private daily bank statements.

Priority 2, liquidity/funding: with the next published financials reconcile opening cash, ₹4.7014 crore warrant deposit, actual project spending, capital advances/creditors, remaining ₹35 crore commitments and debt drawdowns. Separate restricted cash from freely usable resources and current-asset borrowing limits from project finance. Do not include optional ₹14.1043 crore warrant exercise, proposed ITE investment or provisional Gujarat assistance as established money. Trigger a full re-underwrite if a credible downside bridge cannot preserve required operating cash or if funding requires materially worse dilution than modeled.

Priority 3, collections/profit: track the ₹6.4242 crore aged balance, ₹0.4573 crore disputed old balances, ₹5 crore unbilled revenue, customer advances, GST credits and cumulative CFO/PAT. Require cash evidence rather than renewed assertions of recoverability. Investigate further deterioration, unbilled amounts failing to bill/collect, or revenue growth that does not translate into normalized per-share operating earnings.

Priority 4, operational milestones: check GCT renewal/reapplication around the six-month limit from 6 August 2026, agreement/FOIS/weighbridge completion, actual wagon approvals/production, and ICD infrastructure and final customs notifications before the one-year LoI window from 10 September 2026. Compare orders received, executed and remaining instead of repeating a gross order figure. Track realized units, ASPs, customer diversification and utilization versus the latest 10,000 TEU/2,400 wagon claims.

Priority 5, implementation: authenticate latest BSE lot, surveillance/price-band status, 60-session tape and spreads at the user’s actual intended position. The 250-share lot alone makes the nominal ₹5 lakh example discontinuous. No alert or trade is scheduled by this report; these are review triggers.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved, with BQS 5.2 and GQS 5.0 analytical points, IAS NS and all comparative ranking flags false while G2 is unresolved. The business has some attractive operating traits but does not satisfy the framework’s high-quality compounder requirements, notably moat, capital efficiency, cash realization, balance-sheet resilience and sustained execution. Valuation is not used to lower business quality; the funding and price-implied concerns belong in their own factors and gates.

No ordinary entry price, return forecast, position recommendation or order instruction is supplied. Lower valuation alone does not resolve missing project funding or reliability evidence. Reclassification first requires clear group cash/ownership reconciliation, conservative funded phase completion and implementation evidence. If those clear, rerun every annual financing row, the NCI attribution, normalized earnings, lot-aware liquidity and 12/15/18% hurdle cases using the updated share count and price.

For a current holder, the analytical priority is exposure to completion funding, collections and dilution, not an automatic sell or hold instruction without portfolio context. For a prospective buyer, preserve optionality while the specific gates are resolved rather than capitalizing the entire management ambition. This is general company research and scenario analysis, not personalized investment, tax or legal advice, and no claim of guaranteed exit liquidity or investment return is made.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises FY26/FY25 audited annual reports, IPO restated history, earnings-call transcripts, warrant/allotment/correction filings, and underlying railway, Gujarat and customs letters. Public mirrors preserve signed issuer/authority documents with source hashes. Market price and volume are secondary and separately qualified; issuer facts do not rely on the inaccurate secondary articles that confuse eligible project cost with subsidy money, describe future events as completed, or misidentify the exchange. Peer annual reports are used for operating context only.

Safe financial extracts retain fiscal basis, units, source IDs and page locators. FY21–23 are restated standalone, FY24 onward consolidated; no fictional ten-year series is supplied. FY25 prior cost presentation was regrouped: manufacturing/employee reallocations change component labels but not total expense or EBIT. Normalized NOPAT uses a 25.17% assumed tax rate and removes all other income. CAP uses a whole-organic-group bridge including uncommissioned assets and NCI, not an average-ROCE shortcut. Models do not assign probabilities; their growth, unit prices, margins, working capital, cash floor, capital expenditure, exits and rescue financing are explicit assumptions.

Open questions with decision impact: exact KMT ownership and NCI capital/cash reconciliation; consolidated CF classification and AS23 wording; fresh funded phase capex/creditors and facility purpose; whether aged/unbilled receivables collected; permanent GCT permission; final wagon and ICD approvals; reconciled site capacities and product unit economics; current pledge/lock-in/surveillance and full BSE tape. A missing document is not evidence of wrongdoing, and an unmodified audit is not a substitute for the missing quantitative bridge.

Analytical backups intentionally exclude raw PDFs, HTML, OCR, page images and shareholder lists. Their reproduction checks internal calculations from source-safe extracts and exact output hashes, not fresh authentication of original documents. Original public URLs and SHA256 values permit a separate source-authentication step. The full annual funding, valuation, sensitivity and historical rows are embedded in the canonical record rather than hidden behind file references.

evidence.claim: Legal identity is Kalyani Cast-Tech Limited, ISIN INE0N6U01018, BSE SME 544023; 7,180,500 paid shares and 250-share exchange master lot.
evidence.locator: S1 PDF 123; S16 exact ISIN rows
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Interop SM/ST route rows do not establish NSE listing or clear all trading restrictions.

evidence.claim: FY23–26 revenue rose from ₹63.2701 crore to ₹149.9447 crore; 33.32% CAGR. FY26 growth slowed to 7.70%.
evidence.locator: S1 PDF 115; S2 PDF 101; S3 PDF 164
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: FY21–26 68.01% CAGR reflects a COVID/foundry trough and container pivot, not a comparable five-year demand series.

evidence.claim: FY26 goods revenue fell from ₹139.0355 crore to ₹135.8552 crore; services rose to ₹8.6665 crore and unbilled revenue was ₹5 crore.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Do not label the entire sales increase as higher container shipments; no full volume-price bridge.

evidence.claim: Three-year CFO/PAT is 0.4153 and five-year 0.5338; FY26 CFO ₹18.2233 crore contains ₹3.765 crore inventory release and ₹5.8892 crore additional customer advances.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: FY26 alone CFO/PAT 1.065 is a genuine recovery; excluding those two sources leaves ₹8.5691 crore, not a forecast of steady-state CFO.

evidence.claim: FY26 receivables ₹32.9921 crore include ₹6.4242 crore aged 1–2 years, ₹0.4573 crore disputed beyond three years and ₹5 crore unbilled; no doubtful-debt allowance in the ageing table.
evidence.locator: PDF 131 and aggregate corporate debtor schedule PDF 137
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Management considers balances recoverable and attributes March delays partly to West Asia disruptions. The specific 1–2-year bucket cannot be explained solely by March events.

evidence.claim: FY26 operating EBIT excluding other income ₹20.6742 crore; PAT attributable to parent ₹17.08 crore. Mutual-fund gain ₹1.6619 crore versus ₹0.4069 crore prior year. Prior liquidated damages ₹0.8738 crore did not recur.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Removing all other income at normalized tax leaves parent PAT about ₹15.48 crore; not an auditor-restated profit measure.

evidence.claim: Organic whole-group IC bridge gives FY23–26 incremental NOPAT/IC 10.46%, versus 17.20% FY23–25; FY25–26 only 4.20%.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: IC includes uncommissioned CWIP and advances; early-year lag is not persistent value destruction. Capital-cost assumption 13–16%; no attributable mature Gujarat cohort return.

evidence.claim: Full FY26 CARO says bank statements agree with books: HDFC limit ₹23.38 crore and drawn approximately ₹0.578 crore. No default or material fraud reported. Standalone and consolidated IFC opinions are unmodified; explicit audit-trail paragraph says enabled throughout and no tampering identified.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Boilerplate cross-reference to modification at PDF 69 conflicts with the positive explicit audit-trail statement at PDF 71. No numerical bank reconciliation difference is reported, not an independently reconstructed zero.

evidence.claim: FY25 CARO also says quarterly bank statements agree with books, HDFC limit ₹17.45 crore, drawn ₹5.2763 crore; both IFR controls opinions and explicit audit-trail statements are positive.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Audit assurance is not a guarantee; FY25 CARO separately explains ₹0.51 crore KMT subscription paid against a prior-year liability.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated cash flow deducts ₹0.0302 crore NCI profit in CFO and classifies ₹4.0402 crore NCI movement in investing. Algebraic reclassification to inferred ₹4.01 crore external financing preserves net cash. FY25 shows ₹0.4926 crore NCI in investing and ₹0.5847 crore noncurrent-investment outflow despite zero consolidated investment balances.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Net cash reconciliation holds. Parent subscription payment explains part of the history, but no issuer cash-elimination reconciliation was found. This is not proof of missing cash or fraud.

evidence.claim: Consolidation policy refers to equity method/AS23 for KMT although balance-sheet format eliminates parent equity investment and loan. FY26 parent KMT equity ₹10.5 crore and loan ₹12.3971 crore; consolidated NCI ₹4.5328 crore.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: A 70% ownership ratio can be inferred from capital movements, but a confirming FY26 ownership/allotment schedule was not retrieved; model tests 51% and 70%, not wholly owned.

evidence.claim: Issuer corrected its May claim of ₹70 crore invested during FY26: on 8 June it said ₹70 crore was planned, partly spent, with balance intended by 31 July, exclusive of debt funding.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Correction is evidence of clarification, not proof of total deployment or sanctioned project financing. ₹450–500 crore long-term plan and ₹200 crore tied-up claim remain management assertions.

evidence.claim: Gujarat registration describes ₹110 crore project cost and ₹80 crore eligible project cost; authority expressly says provisional registration does not entitle financial assistance.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: No subsidy cash included. ₹70 crore phase, ₹110 crore registered project and ₹450–500 crore campus plan overlap and are not added together.

evidence.claim: Western Railway notification permits temporary non-interlocked GCT operation for six months from 6 August 2026, with agreement and systems matters to complete; first trial train arrived 20 August.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Operational milestone is real; permanent unrestricted operation and recurring commercial utilization are not demonstrated.

evidence.claim: 11 September filing encloses 10 September CBIC approval for issuance of ICD LoI, conditional on operationalization within one year, customs staff, infrastructure and subsequent statutory notifications. Latest filing gives approximately 10,000 TEUs and 2,400 wagons annual capacity; wagon operation still expected, not achieved.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: May letter used 2,500 wagons and a different container scope. Capacity counts/TEUs and campus scope need reconciliation; LoI is not operating customs approval.

evidence.claim: 323,123 warrants at ₹582 allotted 23 September; ₹4.7014397 crore upfront received and ₹14.1043189 crore exercise money remains optional within 18 months. Fully converted shares 7,503,623.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: 4.50% share-count increase means 4.306% existing-holder dilution, not 4.50% dilution. No double counting of initial deposit at exercise.

evidence.claim: Promoter/preferential table gives 59.47% before full exercise and 61.19% after. July and August exchange-requested corrections identify promoter subscriptions and missing percentage columns; issuer says shareholders approved 28 July.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: These are procedural corrections, not an exchange finding of manipulation. Latest pledge/lock-in status not independently authenticated.

evidence.claim: FY26 family-related rents total ₹0.276 crore, legal fees ₹0.072 crore and labour/services ₹0.2567 crore; director remuneration ₹0.8595 crore, up from ₹0.685 crore.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Company states arm’s-length, ordinary-course approvals; audit reports compliance. Directors report says no Section 186 loans/investments although notes/CARO report KMT funding, requiring scope clarification.

evidence.claim: IPO prospectus says top seven customers contributed 97% of FY23 and 96% of FY22 product revenue, without firm long-term minimum purchase commitments.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Current revenue concentration is not disclosed in comparable form. Specialty design relationships are useful but do not remove buyer concentration or raw-material risk.

evidence.claim: June/November 2025 calls describe specialist container designs and domestic substitution. May 2026 letter reports 56 stainless-steel units delivered and a ₹60 crore confirmed order book.
evidence.locator: S4 PDF 3,5; calls business and capacity discussion
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: No independent patent, exclusivity or competitor cost curve established. November ₹140 crore figure included about ₹92.6 crore already executed; it was not an unexecuted ₹140 crore backlog.

evidence.claim: November 2025 management discussed FY26 revenue of ₹180–200 crore. Actual operations revenue was ₹149.94 crore. Gujarat container start and trial train arrived in 2026, but terminal and ICD approvals came after the May June targets.
evidence.locator: FY26 results; call outlook; dated approvals
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Management cites steel increases, selective order refusal and geopolitical collection delays. One-day ceremonial rescheduling is not counted as a material execution miss.

evidence.claim: Titagarh FY25 report discloses 9,431 wagon output and approximately 12,000 annual capacity; Texmaco reports large diversified rolling-stock operations and 23.5% wagon production growth.
evidence.locator: S19 PDF 33, printed 64–65; S20 PDF 6, printed 9
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Peers are larger, diversified and not clean container comparables; no contemporaneous unverified peer P/E median is used to set value.

evidence.claim: 19 October secondary close ₹1,123.85 cross-matches two providers. Official master lot 250; a ₹5 lakh reference buys one lot for ₹280,962.50 below the budget or requires two lots/₹561,925 above it.
evidence.locator: 19 October historical row; exact ISIN master rows
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Not executable quote. Sixty observations imply theoretical capacity but not validated zero-trade calendar, actual traded value, bid-ask spread or current BSE restrictions.

evidence.claim: All three unassisted non-rescue forecasts breach required cash before entry, so ordinary and conditional non-rescue IRRs and entry prices stay null.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: This is not a claim that the issuer actually defaulted. Published March cash, optional warrants and a WC line cannot substantiate unknown project cash commitments alone.

evidence.claim: Separate explicit-rescue models give bear/base/bull five-year IRRs approximately −28.1%/−3.0%/+17.4%, with fees, share issuance and NCI deductions. Base gross funding ₹23.42 crore; outcomes are counterfactual, not ordinary targets.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Multiples, margins, commissioning and financing are assumptions. Base contains terminal scale beyond currently demonstrated capacity and requires additional staged expansion.

evidence.claim: A capital-scaled, funded rescue solver reaches the 15% hurdle only around 47.7% annual core growth, ₹1,573 crore terminal group revenue and about ₹151 crore new equity.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Ordinary implied-growth answer remains null. Valid crossing is checked within 0–60%; it is not a claim that the implied growth is achievable.

evidence.claim: ITE Japan agreement dated 8 September concerns refrigerated containers and technology; reciprocal investment around ₹1 crore each is proposed, with no holding at agreement date.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Not revenue, guaranteed cash funding, controlling ownership or a commercial margin proof.

evidence.claim: Consolidated mutual-fund book amount ₹2.1119 crore versus disclosed aggregate fair value ₹2.00209 crore implies a ₹0.10981 crore difference under its lower-of-cost/fair-value policy.
evidence.locator: PDF 118 note 19 and PDF 124 accounting policy
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: About 0.64% of parent PAT; model uses lower fair value. Not by itself a material reliability failure.
